raw.body:
When using React's `ViewTransition` component in a Next.js application, shared element transitions do not work if the document or any ancestor element has `dir="rtl"`.

The exact same code works correctly when `dir="ltr"` is used.

As a workaround, wrapping the transition element in an ancestor with `dir="ltr"` restores the expected behavior.

React version:

* react: 19.2.0
* react-dom: 19.2.0
* next: 16.2.9

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a Next.js application using React 19 and enable View Transitions.
2. Set `<html dir="rtl">` in the root layout.
3. Create two pages with a shared `<ViewTransition name="box">`.
4. Navigate between the pages.
5. Observe that no shared element transition occurs.
6. Change `dir="rtl"` to `dir="ltr"` and repeat the navigation.

<!--
  Your bug will get fixed much faster if we can run your code and it doesn't
  have dependencies other than React. Issues without reproduction steps or
  code examples may be immediately closed as not actionable.
-->

Link to code example:

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <html dir="rtl">
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

## The current behavior

No shared element transition animation is performed when navigating between pages while `dir="rtl"` is applied. The navigation happens immediately without any transition.

## The expected behavior

Shared element transitions should work regardless of the text direction (`ltr` or `rtl`) applied to the document or ancestor elements.
raw.title: Bug: ViewTransition fails to animate shared elements inside RTL layouts
